# Offer of employment — Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend

## 1. Our offer to you

Dear {{employee.full_name}}, we are glad to offer you the job of Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend at Absa Group. This is a permanent job. Your start date is 1 December 2026. The first 3 months are a probation period.

## 2. Your work

You will work at Riviersonderend, head office. Your main duties are: make contact with customers yourself to meet your sales targets; work with your team, share knowledge and best practice, give useful feedback and help improve how the team works; follow all control, compliance and quality rules; and give excellent service so customers are satisfied. We may also ask you to do other duties that fit this job.

## 3. Hours and pay

You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, over 5 days. Your hours are Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00, with a meal break of 60 minutes. Your basic salary is R18,000.00 per month. We pay by EFT on the 25th of each month. We will deduct PAYE and UIF of 1%. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times your ordinary hourly rate.

## 4. Leave

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave in each 12-month leave cycle. You get 30 days of paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle. Family responsibility leave is 3 days a year. Maternity leave is at least 4 months, and parental leave is 10 days.

## 5. How to accept

This offer stays open until 30 November 2026. Please send us a copy of your ID and your qualifications. If you have questions, email hr@example.co.za.

## 6. Acceptance

I, {{employee.full_name}}, accept this offer on {{date_signed}}.

contract.markdown:
# Contract of employment — Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Riviersonderend (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend. The Employee's duties include: Sales Target : Proactively make self-initiated contact with customers in order to deliver against the required sales targets; Collaboration : Constantly seek to improve ways of working by challenging the status quo and supporting an empowering climate within the team, sharing knowledge, experience, best practice and providing constructive feedback as required.; Compliance and Risk Management: Fulfil all activities in adherence to relevant control and compliance requirements, and quality standards; Customer Experience: To provide service excellence and achieve customer satisfaction. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Riviersonderend, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

## 16. Signatures

Signed at ____________ on {{date_signed}}.

For the Employer: {{employer.signatory}}  ____________________

The Employee: {{employee.full_name}}  ____________________

plain_language.explanation: This says who the two sides of the contract are. One side is your employer, Absa Group, at 1 Main Road, Riviersonderend. The other side is you, named with your identity number and your address.

You are hired as Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend. Your duties are sales targets through your own contact with customers, working with and supporting your team, following control and compliance rules and quality standards, and giving service that satisfies customers. The employer may also ask you to do other reasonable duties that fit this job.
Your job starts on 1 December 2026. It is permanent, so it has no set end date.

Your first 3 months are probation. During this time the employer checks your work against what the job needs, and must give you fair evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling if you need it. At the end of probation the employer may confirm you, extend probation or end your job, and must follow a fair procedure.
You work at Riviersonderend, head office. That is the place named in your contract.

You work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, over 5 days, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60 minute meal break, taken after no more than five hours of work in a row. You also get at least 12 hours of rest in a row each day and at least 36 hours of rest in a row each week.

You are paid a basic salary of R18,000.00 a month, which works out to R103.85 for each ordinary hour. The money is paid by EFT each month on the 25th. There are no other cash payments and no payments in kind.

You only work overtime if you agree to it, and it cannot be more than ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times your ordinary hourly wage, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. Sunday work is paid at double your ordinary wage, or 1.5 times if you normally work Sundays, and public holiday work is paid at double.
PAYE and UIF of 1% will be taken off your pay. No other deduction may be made unless you agree in writing for a specific debt, or the law, a court order or an arbitration award requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave in each 12-month cycle, taken at a time agreed with the employer and no later than six months after the cycle ends. You get 30 days of paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle, but in your first six months it is one day for every 26 days worked; a medical certificate may be asked for if you are off more than two days in a row or more than twice in eight weeks. Maternity leave is at least 4 months in a row, parental leave is 10 days in a row, adoption and commissioning parental leave are as set out in the Act, and family responsibility leave is 3 paid days a year once you have worked longer than four months and at least four days a week.

Either you or the employer can end the contract with written notice: one week if you have worked six months or less, two weeks if more than six months but not more than one year, and four weeks if more than one year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. The employer may still dismiss you immediately for a fair reason using a fair procedure, and both sides may agree to skip notice.
No bargaining council agreement covers this business. No sectoral determination applies either.

You may not share or use the employer's confidential information, or that of its clients and suppliers. This applies while you work there and after you leave. The only exceptions are when you need it to do your job or when the law requires it.
Nothing else is part of this contract. Only the clauses in this document count.

This document is the full agreement on what it covers, and any change must be written down and signed by both of you. If any term gives you less than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, a sectoral determination or a collective agreement, the better term wins. The employer keeps these particulars for three years after your job ends and must explain them to you if you ask.
This is the signature block. The employer's signatory signs for Absa Group, and you sign as the employee. It also records the place and the date of signing.
